items.title: How does the alert's real precision change as the event gets rarer or more common?
items.description: The detector's own accuracy stays fixed at L1's numbers -- a 95% true positive rate and a 5% false positive rate. Only the base rate (how common the real event actually is) changes. Drag the slider down toward L1's own 2% and watch precision fall toward 28% -- then drag it up and see how much rarer the event has to get before the alert becomes nearly useless.

params.name: baseRatePercent
params.label: Base rate of the real event

items.compute: const p = params.baseRatePercent / 100; const tpr = 0.95; const fpr = 0.05; const pAlert = p * tpr + (1 - p) * fpr; const precision = pAlert > 0 ? (p * tpr / pAlert) * 100 : 0; return { precision };

outputs.label: Probability the alert is real when it fires
